title: Bank Deposit Make-Good Credit Amount for an Incorrect Amount
content:
On a Bank Deposit transfer where an incorrect amount was found, the make-good credit is worked out in US dollars from the shortfall in the payout currency.

## Clauses

1. **Payout-currency shortfall.** The payout-currency shortfall is the amount the transfer disclosed to be received less the amount the latest payout actually sent, as the transfer's ledger records it in the payout currency.
2. **Shortfall value.** The shortfall value is the payout-currency shortfall divided by the valuation rate. The valuation rate is the transfer's locked exchange rate.
3. **Make-good credit.** The make-good credit is the shortfall value raised by the goodwill percentage (multiplied by one hundred plus the goodwill percentage, over one hundred), plus the notice credit, plus the transfer-size credit, rounded half up to the cent once at the end. The goodwill percentage is 0 percent; the notice credit and the transfer-size credit are 0.00.
4. **Rounding.** Nothing is rounded before the final amount; the credit is rounded half up to the cent once.

## Worked example (hypothetical transfer)

A Bank Deposit transfer to Mexico disclosed an amount received of 9162.15 pesos at a locked exchange rate of 18.3243; the latest payout actually sent 8700.00 pesos.

| Step | Working | Figure |
|---|---|---|
| Payout-currency shortfall | 9162.15 less 8700.00 | 462.15 pesos |
| Valuation rate | the locked exchange rate | 18.3243 |
| Shortfall value | 462.15 divided by 18.3243 | 25.220608... US dollars |
| Raised by the goodwill percentage | multiplied by one hundred plus 0, over one hundred | 25.220608... |
| Plus the notice credit and the transfer-size credit | plus 0.00 and 0.00 | 25.220608... |
| Make-good credit | rounded half up to the cent | 25.22 |

## Basis questions

**Which payout is compared with the disclosed amount?** The latest payout actually sent on the transfer.

**In which currency is the shortfall measured?** In the payout currency; it becomes US dollars only when divided by the valuation rate.
